metadata.description: Lebanese tax and fiscal legislation: income tax, VAT, customs, property tax, stamp duty

laws.official_title_french: Décret-loi No. 144/1959 - Impôt sur le Revenu

amendments.summary: Authorized banks to set aside provisions for doubtful debts.
Tax rates and brackets have been modified through annual budget laws.

key_articles.text_english: Tax on profits from industrial, commercial, and non-commercial professions. Schedular system: profits from trade/industry, profits from professions, salaries/wages, movable capital income.
key_articles.subject: Tax categories

key_articles.text_english: Tax on salaries, wages, and pensions. Employer withholding obligations.
key_articles.subject: Salary tax

key_articles.text_english: Tax on income from movable capital: interest, dividends, investment returns.
key_articles.subject: Capital income tax

laws.historical_context: Lebanon's income tax system is a schedular (cedular) system where different types of income are taxed separately rather than aggregated. There is no unified personal income tax. Tax rates are relatively low compared to regional and international averages, reflecting Lebanon's traditionally liberal economic model. The system has been criticized for its regressive nature and weak enforcement.

laws.official_title_french: Loi No. 379/2001 - Taxe sur la Valeur Ajoutée (TVA)

amendments.summary: VAT rate increased from 10% to 11% via Law No. 64/2017 (2017 budget).

key_articles.text_english: Scope: VAT applies to supply of goods and services in Lebanon, and importation of goods. Standard rate: 11%.
key_articles.subject: Scope and rate

laws.historical_context: Introduced in 2002 at a rate of 10%, later increased to 11%. Replaced the consumption tax system. Registration threshold applies for businesses with turnover above a set threshold. Exemptions include financial services, education, and certain basic food items. Administration by the VAT Directorate within the Ministry of Finance.

Imposes stamp duty on various legal documents, contracts, receipts, and official papers. Rates vary by document type. A significant source of government revenue and a common feature of Lebanese administrative processes.

Governs customs duties, import/export procedures, transit goods, customs zones, and enforcement. Lebanon has been in accession negotiations with the WTO and has bilateral trade agreements affecting customs rates. Customs revenue has historically been a major source of government income.

Unified and simplified tax procedures across income tax, VAT, and other fiscal obligations. Implementing decree No. 2488 of July 3, 2009. Streamlined tax filing, assessment, objection, and collection procedures.

laws.official_title_french: Loi No. 43/2015 - Échange de Renseignements Fiscaux
laws.historical_context: Enacted to comply with international standards on tax transparency (OECD/Global Forum). Allows exchange of tax-related information with treaty partner countries. Significant in the context of Lebanon's banking secrecy tradition.

Annual budget laws authorize government spending and often contain tax rate modifications. Lebanon notably failed to pass a budget from 2005 to 2017 (12 years), operating on extended twelve-monthly budgets. A budget was finally passed in 2017 (Law No. 64/2017), followed by the 2018 and 2019 budgets. Budget laws often include fiscal provisions that amend tax rates and thresholds.
